name: Battle of Pharsalus
intro: The plain of Pharsalus in Thessaly, in August, during the civil war. You are Julius Caesar, with about 22,000 veteran legionaries and 1,000 cavalry. Pompey the Great, defender of the Senate, has perhaps 36,000 to 45,000 legionaries and 5,000 to 7,000 cavalry under Labienus.
debrief: In reality, Pompey came down from his hill as Caesar’s army was about to march off, and Caesar accepted battle. The river Enipeus covered one flank. Pompey massed his cavalry on his left to sweep round Caesar’s right and ordered his infantry to stand still and receive the charge. Caesar thinned his lines to match Pompey’s front and hid a fourth line of cohorts behind his right, told to thrust their pila at the horsemen’s faces. Caesar’s veterans halted short of the enemy to catch their breath before charging. When Labienus’s cavalry drove back Caesar’s horse, the fourth line charged and routed it; Caesar’s cavalry and third line then rolled up Pompey’s left, and Pompey fled to his camp and then to Egypt, where he was killed. Caesar claims to have lost only about 200 men; another account gives 1,200, and Pompeian losses are put at 6,000 to 15,000 dead and 24,000 captured. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: Pompey’s cavalry flees for the hills.
His left wing is rolled up.

decisions.title: Pompey comes down
decisions.text: For days Pompey has stayed on his hill. This morning your army was about to march off, when his army came down onto the plain. He has twice your infantry and six times your cavalry.

hint.text: Your men are veterans of Gaul. His are many and fresh.

scout.text: Pompey has offered battle on the plain at last. Your veterans are at their best in an open fight; if you march off, the chance may not come again.

choices.label: Turn the army round and accept battle

fx.text: Caesar halts the march. ‘We must put off our march and think of battle, as we have always wanted,’ he says. The army turns to face Pompey.

choices.label: March on as planned toward fresh supplies

fx.text: You march away. Pompey follows, and the chance passes.

choices.label: Stay in camp until he is further from his own

fx.text: Pompey will not attack your camp.

decisions.title: Drawing up the line
decisions.text: The river Enipeus covers your left. Pompey’s line is deeper and longer. Most of his cavalry, with his archers and slingers, is massed on his left, facing your right.

hint.text: Pompey means his cavalry to sweep round your right flank.

scout.text: Anchor your left on the river and thin your lines to match his frontage. Your right needs special care.

choices.label: Anchor on the river; thin your lines

fx.text: Your cohorts stretch to match Pompey’s line, the river on your left, the Tenth on your right.

choices.label: Keep the lines deep and accept a shorter front

fx.text: Your line is solid, but Pompey overlaps both ends of it.

choices.label: Move to open ground where veterans can manoeuvre

fx.text: Your left is now open as well as your right.

decisions.title: Crastinus
decisions.text: Gaius Crastinus, a veteran centurion who once led the first cohort of the Tenth, steps forward. He asks to open the attack with 120 volunteers. ‘General,’ he says, ‘today I will earn your thanks, alive or dead.’

hint.text: The men around Crastinus are cheering.

scout.text: Veterans follow a man like Crastinus anywhere. A first charge led by him will put heart into the whole line, though he may not survive it.

choices.label: Let Crastinus and his volunteers lead the charge

fx.text: Crastinus runs forward at the head of his volunteers, and the whole line follows him with a roar. He will be found among the dead, killed by a sword thrust to the face.

choices.label: Keep him in his place: the line matters more than one man

fx.text: Crastinus obeys. The line advances steadily, without his fire.

choices.label: Keep your best centurion safe to guard the camp

fx.text: The veterans grumble as their best centurion is sent to the rear.

decisions.title: The fourth line
decisions.text: You have a few cohorts to spare from your third line.

hint.text: His cavalry will come at your right. Your own horse is too few to stop it.

scout.text: Six cohorts, hidden behind your right wing, can meet the cavalry when it comes. Told to thrust their pila into the riders’ faces, not throw them, they will panic young aristocrats on horseback.

choices.label: Hide the cohorts as a fourth line behind the right

fx.text: Six cohorts slip behind your right wing, out of sight. They are told to use their pila as spears, at the horsemen’s faces.

choices.label: Put the cohorts in the front line to lengthen it

fx.text: The front is thicker, but nothing is held back for the cavalry.

choices.label: Keep them as a last reserve by the camp

fx.text: They are safe and useless.

decisions.title: The charge
decisions.text: Pompey’s infantry has been ordered to stand still and wait for your charge, hoping your men will tire running the long gap. Your line begins to advance.

scout.text: Veterans know what to do: halt short of the enemy, catch their breath and dress the ranks, then charge the last stretch and throw.

choices.label: Halt halfway to catch breath, then charge

fx.text: Your veterans see the trick. They halt, get their breath, dress the line, then charge, throw their pila and draw swords. Pompey’s line is pushed back.
Your line charges home.

choices.label: Charge straight across while the men are eager

fx.text: Your men arrive blown and ragged.

choices.label: Halt and make them come to you

fx.text: Neither side moves.

decisions.title: Labienus’s cavalry
decisions.text: Labienus leads the Pompeian cavalry forward. It drives your horse back and begins to sweep round your right wing.

hint.text: The cavalry is swinging round the Tenth.

scout.text: Now is the moment: reveal the fourth line, then send in the third line and your rallied horse against Pompey’s exposed left.

choices.label: Unleash the hidden line at the cavalry

fx.text: The fourth line charges the horsemen, thrusting at their faces. They panic and flee for the hills. Caesar’s horse wheels round Pompey’s left, the third line goes in, and Pompey’s army breaks. Pompey flees to his camp, and then from it.
Your right is pushed back, but holds.

choices.label: Pull the Tenth back to face the cavalry

fx.text: The cavalry is held off, but your line bends.

choices.label: Push the infantry; win in the centre before the cavalry tells

fx.text: Labienus’s horse falls on your rear.

quotes.who: Caesar, looking over the Pompeian dead

quotes.text: Today, general, I will earn your thanks, alive or dead.
quotes.who: The centurion Crastinus, before the first charge
